newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African employers bemoan employment proposals.
newsitem.headline: S.African employers bemoan employment proposals.

text.p: South Africa's Afrikaanse Handelsinstituut (AHI) business grouping on Thursday criticised a controversial new employment bill launched by Labour Minister Tito Mboweni, which was backed by the cabinet this week.
Saying industry leaders feared the legislation proposed by Mboweni could raise labour costs, AHI President Theo van Wyk added that industry leaders had hoped for less extensive regulation.

"The AHI favours basic standards to the extent that they are necessary to protect the average worker, (but) the bill proposes a number of changes which can directly affect labour costs," he said in a statement.
Employers wanted more employee benefits to be negotiated through collective bargaining, rather than enshrined in the bill, he added.

The Basic Conditions of Employment Bill seeks to reduce weekly working hours to 45 from 46 hours, increase overtime pay to time-and-a-half from time-and-a-third, offer workers four months maternity leave instead of the present 12 weeks and double pay for employees who work on Sundays.
The bill will be negotiated between government, business and labour in May, before it is tabled in parliament for approval.
